chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Wassa, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi 'Abdillah, who said:

I asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who is praying and a woman is by his side, to his right or to his left. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it if she is not praying.'

key_terms.بِحِذَاءِهِ: by his side / parallel to him
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no problem with it / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a woman to stand next to a man during his prayer?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* through the chain of Aban ibn Uthman, this hadith clarifies that a woman standing parallel to a man is permissible as long as she is not praying, distinguishing this arrangement from the stricter rules regarding her praying behind him. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic view that the primary concern is avoiding the distraction of the man or the invalidation of the woman's prayer due to proximity, rather than a fixed spatial hierarchy. It underscores the flexibility in prayer arrangements within the family unit while maintaining the integrity of the individual acts of worship.
